$comment: The release-specific half of the converge gate (spec §12.4, template §3e 4).
EDIT THIS FILE IN EVERY RELEASE THAT CHANGES THE API CONTRACT. A version
match cannot detect a new static frontend talking to an old in-memory schema:
both report the new CACHE_VERSION and conditions 1/2/3/6 all pass while the
app is broken. The only thing that catches it is asserting that a key THIS
release added is in the LIVE response — so a release that adds no key has
nothing to add here, and the v0.7.0 example below is the case that proves it.
Shape: one entry per endpoint, with the keys its response must carry. Remove
a key only when the release that introduced it is two releases back. Adding a
key you did not add is worse than adding none — it hides a regression behind a
key that was always there.
`$release` is the release that INTRODUCED the keys named in that entry, not the
current release. It is the clock the removal rule above runs on, so it moves only
when the keys move: a release that adds an endpoint key updates the `$release` of
the entry it touches, and a client-only release correctly leaves every label
where it is. v0.7.0 is the worked example — cf39101 fixed the per-date cook-log
revision and the Back scroll restore in the frontend and added no endpoint key,
so the three v0.6.0 labels are not stale, they are accurate. Relabelling them
v0.7.0 would claim a release introduced keys it did not and would push the
removal of those keys one release out.
`require_deployed` defaults to true, so a run without --deployed-origin is
reported UNPROVEN rather than passing on the local half alone.
